item.title: TYSON WEEKLY RECAP
item.description: Another week down in the Kansas Legislature. Senator Caryn Tyson says the budget barely passed the Senate. She says she voted ‘no’ because it spends more than the state is taking in. She also has a couple other topics the Senate has discussed: The House continues discussion on many topics this week. The Senate Transportation Committee will be hearing about House Bill 24-71 which would rename a portion of I-35 in Franklin County as the Sam Smith Memorial Highway.

item.title: MENTAL HEALTH ADVOCACY
item.description: Yesterday, March 9th was Mental Health Advocacy Day at the State Capital in Topeka. Hundreds of people gathered to tell their story and advocate for the State Legislature to fund mental health facilities. One piece of legislation that may impact the mentally impaired communities is SB 363, which would require KANCARE recipients to recertify every three months. item.title: VITT COBBS ON SPED NUMBERS
item.description: A significant portion of the USD 290 School Board Meeting last night, March 9th, was devoted to special education, particularly at the pre-school level. Special Education Director, Joe Vitt, says despite decreases in total enrollment, special education numbers are not going down: …and with that, state funding has dropped. Superintendent Dr. Ryan Cobbs: Cobbs added that the need for more pre-school education programs, by every school district, has jumped the past several years.

item.title: MILLER ON MAKE MY MOVE
item.description: In the fall of 2025, the Ottawa Chamber of Commerce was awarded nearly $150,000 from the “Home In The Heartland” grant program. Chamber Director, Ryland Miller, says it’s part of a bigger program called “Make My Move” which would showcase Ottawa on a national level, trying to get people to move to Ottawa: Miller will give an update on on the “Make My Move” program at tomorrows Ottawa City Commission meeting. The meeting is at 4:00 at City Hall.

item.title: DOUBLE STABBING IN RICHMOND
item.description: A double stabbing in Richmond this morning, left one person with critical injuries and another in a hospital. Details are not known about how the altercation at the Richmond Body Shop started. The call came in just after 11:00 this morning, according to scanner traffic. One person required an air ambulance for their injuries. The air ambulance landed shortly before noon to transport the patient to an area trauma unit. item.title: Michael Lloyd Perkins
item.description: Michael Lloyd Perkins was born on July 8, 1958, to Richard and Margaret (La Page) Perkins in Plattsburg, New York.
